If you would like to hone your teaching, need an excuse to perfect your cRaft, or want to show off a cool R trick you learned, shoot us an email and we can add your presentation to our calendar <https://d-rug.github.io/calendar.html>! Presentations can be in-person or virtual (and in-person presentations will be streamed for virtual attendees).

messages.subject: problem using ulam() and log_lik=TRUE for rethinking package
messages.subject_clean: problem using ulam() and log_lik=TRUE for rethinking package
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I'm wondering if someone can help me out with an issue I'm having.

I'm using ulam() for a bayesian model and it runs fine when I don't have log_lik=TRUE in it but once I add that in I get an error.

Here is my model:

diverse_f1 <-ulam(alist(
+   grossProd ~ dnorm(mu, sigma),
+   mu <- a +  b*(zScore),
+   zScore~dnorm(mu_x1, sigma_x1),
+   a ~ dnorm(2, 30),
+   b ~ dnorm(0, 100),
+   mu_x1~dnorm(0,100),
+   sigma_x1~dcauchy(0,2),
+   sigma ~ dcauchy(0,2)
+ ),data=d_full_f1,log_lik=TRUE,chains=4 , cores=4 ,start=list( B_impute = rep(0.5,26)))

Here is the error (ran on one chain for debug purposes, see error below....):
no parameter log_lik; sampling not done
no parameter log_lik; sampling not done
no parameter log_lik; sampling not done
no parameter log_lik; sampling not done
here are whatever error messages were returned
[[1]]
Stan model 'anon_model' does not contain samples.

[[2]]
Stan model 'anon_model' does not contain samples.

[[3]]
Stan model 'anon_model' does not contain samples.

[[4]]
Stan model 'anon_model' does not contain samples.

Stan model 'anon_model' does not contain samples.
Error in validObject(.Object) :
  invalid class “ulam” object: invalid object for slot "coef" in class "ulam": got class "NULL", should be or extend class "numeric"
In addition: Warning message:
In .local(object, ...) :
  some chains had errors; consider specifying chains = 1 to debug

Error on one chain:
no parameter log_lik; sampling not done
Stan model 'anon_model' does not contain samples.
Error in validObject(.Object) :
  invalid class “ulam” object: invalid object for slot "coef" in class "ulam": got class "NULL", should be or extend class "numeric"

Any insight would be greatly appreciated!

Best,
Hannah
--
Hannah Waterhouse, PhD
Pronouns: She/Her
Soils and Biogeochemistry Graduate Group
University of California, Davis

messages.body_plain:
Hi Hannah,
I copied your question to the current D-RUG question forum, where it is more likely to be seen. Here is a link:  https://d-rug.discourse.group/t/stan-error-model-doesnt-sample/1506

I've tried to recreate your specific error, but without luck. It could be because I had to make up some toy data in order to test it. However, I do see at least one problem in your code: Your model includes no parameter called "B_impute", so the bit about "start=list( B_impute = rep(0.5,26))" can't do anything for you - I'd recommend deleting that.

Finally, a lot of people have been having problems with rstan, and it sounds like cmdstanr is generally preferred nowadays. In order to use cmdstanr, run this in R:

remotes::install_github( "stan-dev/cmdstanr" )
library( "cmdstanr" )
install_cmdstan()

Then, add this to your ulam() call, after chains=4: cmdstan=TRUE.

Let me know if that helps.
-W

Here's your weekly reminder that D-RUG will be hosting a 2-hour work group tomorrow, from 10-noon in the Data Lab classroom and on zoom. We will be meeting in a hybrid format, in 360 Shields Library (DataLab classroom) and on Zoom <https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862>. You are cordially invited to attend in either venue.

This year, we are adopting a new queueing approach for virtual folks seeking help at D-RUG. If you are joining virtually, we ask that you submit your question to our Discourse site <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> in advance of our meetings, and we will address folks' questions in the order they are received. Of course, you are always welcome (and encouraged) to just come hang out, and use the work group time as a dedicated chunk of time to get some coding done with good company.

For those not familiar with D-RUG, the R Users' Group is a weekly working group to get some help with R-specific coding problems. The coordinators are various and sundry coding connoisseurs, ranging from UCD data scientists to grad students on campus. We meet for 2 hours in an open-forum format, so you can treat D-RUG as a communal, co-working environment: come hang out and chat, work on your own, seek help, make friends. Or, a little bit of everything! Check out our website <https://d-rug.github.io/> for more information.

We are also seeking presenters! It is nice to mix things up with occasional presentations. messages.body_plain:
Anyone who is really into the combination of ecology and statistics should apply to this postdoc (posting closes on 1 December).

I was a postdoc in David's lab and can say that it is a very good lab with a brilliant team. He has a big network of collaborators, as well. Finally, Sydney's eastern suburbs are incredibly beautiful, Australian postdocs are well-paid, and time on this job would count toward the five years needed for permanent residency.
-W

messages.subject: GSR job in "Digital Communications" at UC Davis DataLab
messages.subject_clean: GSR job in "Digital Communications" at UC Davis DataLab
messages.body_plain:
Hi useRs,

Our amazing GSR at DataLab has been awarded an extramural fellowship and will be leaving us at the end of this quarter. So, we have a job opening! If you are a graduate student at UC Davis looking for a position I hope you will consider applying, and/or help spread the word about this opportunity. Details and full job description link below.

Wishing you a restful Thanksgiving holiday!

-

UC Davis DataLab is hiring a GSR in Digital Communications for winter-spring 2022, with possibility of extension into the 2022-2023 academic year. This position requires very strong writing and communication skills, basic familiarity with R, comfort using or learning web platforms (primarily Wordpress); web programming skills and past interdisciplinary research experience are a plus. Students from any graduate group/program are eligible to apply.

Full details and how to apply:   https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/2021/11/10/gsr-digital-comms-2022/

Applications are being reviewing as they are received, so we encourage prospective applicants to submit their materials as soon as possible.

--

Pamela L. Reynolds, PhD

Associate Director

DataLab: Data Science and Informatics

University of California, Davis

plrey...@ucdavis.edu
https://datalab.ucdavis.edu
